text:
Done across 4998e98 (web) and ec9e86b (android). Both clients: 5s sync while a list is open and the app/tab is active, plus strike-through -> 120ms hold -> 180ms slide toward the inline start, only when 'show checked' is off.

Three bugs the work surfaced, all now covered by tests and all shared between the two implementations because they share a design:
1. Hooks placed after an early return (web) — a list that failed to resolve changed the hook count between renders.
2. Toggling 'show checked' OFF animated every checked row away at once. That is a view change, not a check-off; sliding twenty rows out is slow and misrepresents what happened. Both clients now re-baseline silently.
3. A row unchecked mid-animation rendered twice — once live, once as a ghost.

The Android live-sync test asserts the loop goes SILENT after cancellation, not just that it fires on schedule. If repeatOnLifecycle did not behave as documented the symptom would be a phone syncing every 5s in a pocket for hours — which users report as 'bad battery', never as a bug, so it needed pinning explicitly.

SSE/WebSocket stays rejected, not deferred: a held connection occupies a WSGI worker for its whole life and this server is a blueprint mounted in someone else's host app, which cannot dictate the worker class. Measured justification for polling instead: an already-up-to-date /sync against a 60-item list costs 3.66 ms, so two shoppers at 5s are under 0.25% of one core.
